He had challenged the rejection of his discharge application. “The perusal of the FIR would show that the complainant/victim has identified herself to be a woman and the aforesaid self determination cannot be questioned at least at the present stage while accused is seeking discharge,” the judge said. Justice Mehroz K Pathan He concluded that “allegations of assault and outraging the modesty of a woman can be sustained even where the victim is a transgender person who identifies herself as a woman.” The accused, an Agniveer in the Indian Army, faced charges under Section 75 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) and Section 18(D) of the Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019.
